latest_release.name: DroidDeck 0.7.11
latest_release.body:
**DroidDeck is 100% open source. No ads. No subscriptions. No telemetry. No proprietary components. No source withheld.** Since 0.7.1: **42 contributors** | **467 pull requests** | **111 of them from 39 outside contributors**. We are so grateful for you all! 0.7.11 is the convenience store release. **EA, Ubisoft Connect and Rockstar Games** join the Stores tab, with no launchers to install and cloud saves for EA and Ubisoft. Steam, games, the desktop and the Terminal now **run directly on Android with no proot**, which cuts CPU overhead and gives much better 1% lows. **Zero-copy presentation** sends frames straight to the display and brings real HDR. Games on a memory card start about 4X faster. Around those sit a rebuilt Library, a tab bar you can rearrange, Settings with search, a smoother first run, and many smaller conveniences. The details are below. ### Features - **A new foundation.** 0.7.11 reworks the stack that runs your games, from how Linux runs on Android to how frames reach the screen: - **No proot by default.** Steam, Proton games, the desktop and the Terminal run directly on Android, with lower CPU overhead and much better 1% lows. (@xXJSONDeruloXx, @maxjivi05, @K11MCH1, [#2300](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2300), [#2522](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2522), [#2560](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2560), [#3041](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/3041)) - **Zero-copy presentation** With DD-Turnip v0.9.0 or newer, frames reach the display without an extra copy: improving frametimes, frame pacing, and drastically reducing cases of dropped frames. (@maxjivi05, [#2905](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2905)) - **DroidDeck-Bionic**, a new test build that runs the game itself on Android’s own libc, with lower memory use, better compatibility and, in some games, better performance. (@The412Banner, [#3037](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/3037))

- Added **EA, Ubisoft Connect and Rockstar Games** stores: sign in, browse, download and launch without their launchers. EA and Ubisoft get cloud saves. (@xXJSONDeruloXx, @K11MCH1, @maxjivi05, [#2259](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2259), [#2527](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2527), [#2521](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2521), [#2438](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2438), [#2440](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2440), [#2486](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2486), [#23

detail.readme:
DroidDeck brings the SteamOS experience to Android: Steam Gaming Mode, full Linux desktop, integration with GOG, Epic Games, Xbox, and other storefronts, Steam VR, and more!

100% open source. No ads. No Subscriptions. No telemetry. No proprietary components. No source withheld.

> The official website is [droid-deck.dev](https://droid-deck.dev). Only download DroidDeck from this repository's [Releases](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/releases).

## Install 1. Android 9 or newer on Adreno 730 or newer, or any 8xx. Adreno 6xx, Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR are experimental. Adreno 710 is currently unsupported. No root needed. 2. About 3 GB free for the runtime, plus 1.1 GB for the desktop and emulators. 3. Install the [APK](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/releases/download/0.7.11/DroidDeck-0.7.11.apk), install the Linux runtime, press **Play** and sign in to Steam. 4. On Android 14 and newer, turn on **Disable child process restrictions** in Developer options. On Android 12 and 13, Steam's first launch shows a **Fix it for me** button that walks you through it. Smart glasses setup is in the [support matrix](docs/smart-glasses-support.md). Release notes are in [docs/releases](docs/releases). Help, Preview builds and device reports are on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JRGAvawjsm). For bugs, post in **#bug-reports** with the zip from **Share logs**. ## Build Needs Docker, Java 17, the Android SDK and NDK, Rust via rustup, Go, a host C compiler, the x86_64 and i686 MinGW-w64 compilers (i686 with DWARF-2 exceptions, as Debian and Ubuntu ship it; SJLJ builds such as Homebrew's cannot link Rust's `i686-pc-windows-gnu`), GitHub CLI, Python 3 and `zstd`. On x86_64 Linux, Docker also needs an arm64 binfmt handler (`docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64`). ```bash tools/build_local.sh ``` The APK lands in `app/build/outputs/apk/release/`. Install it with `tools/deploy_local.sh`. After the first run, `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease` reuses the prepared inputs. Unit tests run with `./gradlew -PskipRust=true :app:testDebugUnitTest`, and the helper and preload suite with `bash tools/test_local.sh`. On Windows, see `tools/run_windows.ps1` and `tools/prepare_windows_runtime.py`. ## Credits and licence DroidDeck is [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Steam and Proton belong to Valve Corporation. VITURE, RayNeo, XREAL, Rokid, REDMAGIC, Nintendo Switch and Joy-Con are trademarks of their owners. This project is not affiliated with any of them.
Runtime, Wine and Proton - Runtime, shim, input and controller work build on WinNative and Bannerlator by maxjivi05. - mmap ring buffer controller input by ribbit384 ([WinNative #345](https://github.com/WinNative-Emu/WinNative/pull/345)). - [FEX](https://github.com/FEX-Emu/FEX) (MIT) runs x86 code. DroidDeck's build puts the platform name under `AT_PLATFORM` so [sharun](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun) AppImages by VHSgunzo (MIT) start through its [userland-execve](https://crates.io/crates/userland-execve) loader (MIT), and its GL thunk hands X errors to the program's own error handler. FEX's code disk cache was checked in its source. The fix for host stack left behind when a program leaves a signal handler without returning follows the approach suggested in [FEX-Emu/FEX#2487](https://github.com/FEX-Emu/FEX/issues/2487). The host stack fix for system calls that end a block is a backport of Ryan Houdek's [FEX-Emu/FEX#6122](https://github.com/FEX-Emu/FEX/pull/6122). - x86 AppImages, and arm64 ones whose runtime can't unpack on Android, are unpacked with [uruntime](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/uruntime) by VHSgunzo (MIT), shipped unmodified with its licence. - DwarFS AppImages are unpacked without proot by `dwarfsextract` from [DwarFS](https://github.com/mhx/dwarfs) by Marcus Holland-Moritz (MIT), the release binary uruntime embeds, taken out of its self-extracting wrapper and shipped with its licence. - x86 programs linking OpenSSL 3 use the copy in the [Steam Linux Runtime 4.0](https://gitlab.steamos.cloud/steamrt/steamrt). x86 Linux games get the `/etc/asound.conf` that [pressure-vessel](https://gitlab.steamos.cloud/steamrt/steam-runtime-tools) writes. - `WriteProcessMemory` hooks fall back to `/proc//mem` the way [Wine](https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine)'s `server/ptrace.c` did before Wine 11. - Windows programs on noexec storage get executable copies of their image pages, following [@yujikaido](https://github.com/yujikaido)'s finding in [droiddeck-rp4pro](https://github.com/yujikaido/droiddeck-rp4pro) that Wine's own processes need the noexec shim. - Wine write watches use userfaultfd support in [Proton](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/wine)'s `dlls/ntdll/unix/virtual.c` (LGPL-2.1-or-later). libddsession supplies the arm64 syscall number and answers `PAGEMAP_SCAN` from `/proc/self/pagemap`. - libddsession runs Wine's arm64 `SIGUSR2` context handler (`dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_arm64.c`, LGPL-2.1-or-later) in place on a frame laid out like [Linux](https://github.com/torvalds/linux)'s `arch/arm64/kernel/signal.c`, and serves `fill_vm_counters` in `dlls/ntdll/unix/process.c` the kernel's own `/proc//status`. - droiddeck-ntsync follows the [Linux](https://github.com/torvalds/linux) ntsync semantics in `Documentation/userspace-api/ntsync.rst` (GPL-2.0). - The proot fast path orders bindings like [PRoot](https://github.com/proot-me/proot)'s `path/binding.c` (GPL-2.0-or-later). - DiRT 3 and DiRT Showdown keep their telemetry socket the way RoccoC's DiRTTelemetryErrorFix (MIT) does, based on the fix by Carsten Gottschling. - Zink on PowerVR keeps colour textures in colour with Icenowy Zheng's upstream [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa) fix d55418dae7 (MIT), carried as a runtime patch. - Games and AppImage, Flatpak and Snap programs such as emulators use `TU_DEBUG=sysmem` by default, as does the Steam client. Turnip sysmem rendering can be turned off in Performance settings, except with the Adreno 710/720 driver, which always uses it. - Black Ops III and Dark Souls Remastered start without [umu-protonfixes](https://github.com/Open-Wine-Components/umu-protonfixes) (BSD-2-Clause), whose `311210.py` and `570940.py` fail under ARM64 Proton. - [ReSkate](https://github.com/Dingo-Shenanigans/ReSkate) (GPL-3.0) by Dingo Shenanigans uses the launch option from its README and D3D12 feature level 12_1. - The arm64 client's sign in was checked by reading Steam's saved token with the `ConnectCache` format from [deadlock-api-ingest](https://github.com/deadlock-api/deadlock-api-ingest).
Stores - Epic Games and GOG build on [Phobos](https://github.com/phobos665)'s adaptation of [Legendary](https://github.com/legendary-gl/legendary) and [gogdl](https://github.com/Heroic-Games-Launcher/heroic-gogdl). GOG install script registry entries are read the way [Heroic Games Launcher](https://github.com/Heroic-Games-Launcher/HeroicGamesLauncher) (GPL-3.0) reads them. GOG cloud storage requests send the Galaxy communication-service User-Agent that gogdl and [Lutris](https://github.com/lutris/lutris) (GPL-3.0) send. Deleted GOG cloud saves are recognised by the empty-gzip deletion hash gogdl and Lutris skip. - Epic's official Linux launcher preview runs through FEX. That setup is outside Epic's listed Linux support. - The launcher's .deb gets the WebKitGTK and GTK 3 libraries it needs from unmodified [Debian](https://www.debian.org) 13 packages, following [@zooluis](https://github.com/zooluis)'s research in [#2268](https://github.com/Droid-Deck/DroidDeck/pull/2268). - Battle.net is by [@kayakyakr](https://github.com/kayakyakr). It runs Blizzard's own client in Proton (downloaded from Blizzard, not included) and shows key art from the [Battle.net Shop](https://shop.battle.net). Without Steam, its games see the pad as an Xbox 360 controller via `PROTON_SPOOF_STEAMINPUT_VIDPID` in [Proton](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/wine)'s `dlls/winebus.sys`. - The EA store follows the EA app's protocols as documented by [ArmchairDevelopers](https://github.com/ArmchairDevelopers)' [Maxima](https://github.com/ArmchairDevelopers/Maxima) (GPL-3.0): sign-in, the GraphQL queries (included verbatim, since EA matches them by hash), build archives, online activation licences and the LSX game endpoint. The code is DroidDeck's own. - Battle.net installs drive Blizzard's Agent the way [@barncastle](https://github.com/barncastle)'s [Battle.Net-Installer](https://github.com/barncastle/Battle.Net-Installer) does, with requests from [wowdev.wiki](https://wowdev.wiki/Agent). Read without taking code: [@mubaraknumann](https://github.com/mubaraknumann)'s [unifideck](https://github.com/mubaraknumann/unifideck), [@djmittens](https://github.com/djmittens)'s [neo-mittens](https://github.com/djmittens/neo-mittens) `bnetswitch`, [@BCD1210](https://github.com/BCD1210)'s [soju](https://github.com/BCD1210/soju) and [Lutris](https://github.com/lutris/lutris)'s `product.db` reader. - The Rockstar launcher service looks for launcher pipe names in the executables beside the game, since [CitizenFX](https://github.com/citizenfx/fivem)'s `ros-patches-five` shows GTA V opening `GTAVLauncher_Pipe` and [@pingod](https://github.com/pingod)'s [rdr2-linux-launcher](https://github.com/pingod/rdr2-linux-launcher) notes that Rockstar's protected executables resolve such strings only at run time. Read without taking code. - World of Warcraft addon imports replace an addon's folder from a temporary copy, as [WowUp](https://github.com/WowUp/WowUp) does, and read flavour folders the way [WoWDeck](https://github.com/sigboe/wowdeck) does. No code from either is used. - The World of Warcraft addon Download window searches [WoWInterface](https://www.wowinterface.com) through its MMOUI API. Installed addons show their `.toc` version and `X-WoWI-ID`, and are checked against that list for updates, as [WowUp](https://github.com/WowUp/WowUp) does. The Addons tab installs the official [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/download/app) Linux app from CurseForge's own update feed (downloaded at install time and checked against its SHA-512, not included), which keeps its own sign-in. - The Xbox store runs [@domsvoboda](https://github.com/domsvoboda)'s [nexus-backend](https://github.com/domsvoboda/nexus-backend) 0.2.15 (GPL-3.0, a fork of [Xodus](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/xodus)), and Xbox games load the Windows modules of his [nexus-runtime](https://github.com/domsvoboda/nexus-runtime) (LGPL-2.1-or-later), including the C++ [nexus-xgameruntime](https://github.com/domsvoboda/nexus-xgameruntime) and `wintypes.dll`. Content licensing sends delegation-compact device tickets in the licensing wire form, as nexus-backend's Store license path (commit `27c335e`) does. Minecraft's GameInput setup was checked against [@Wyze3306](https://github.com/Wyze3306)'s [BedrockOnLinux](https://github.com/Wyze3306/BedrockOnLinux) (MIT). - The Xbox Cloud Gaming player uses the WebRTC client of [@unknownskl](https://github.com/unknownskl)'s [Greenlight](https://github.com/unknownskl/greenlight) (MIT), and its offer tweaks and sharpening follow [@redphx](https://github.com/redphx)'s [Better xCloud](https://github.com/redphx/better-xcloud) (MIT). See `tools/xcloud-player/NOTICE.md`. - The itch.io butler pack ships butler's `7z.so`, itch.io's build of [7-Zip](https://www.7-zip.org) by Igor Pavlov (LGPL-2.1, unRAR restriction on RAR code), unmodified. Other archives use Apache Commons Compress and the runtime's bsdtar (libarchive). - The Store uses [Flatpak](https://github.com/flatpak/flatpak) (LGPL-2.1) through DroidDeck's own bubblewrap shim. Chromium and Electron apps start directly, since [zypak](https://github.com/refi64/zypak) by [@refi64](https://github.com/refi64) (BSD-3-Clause) always uses Flatpak's spawn portal. - Folder sync runs [Syncthing](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing) (MPL-2.0), built from [@researchxxl](https://github.com/researchxxl)'s [syncthing-android](https://github.com/researchxxl/syncthing-android) fork (MPL-2.0).
Audio, video and HUD - Steam audio goes through [@The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner)'s [DirectAudio](https://github.com/The412Banner/directaudio) PulseAudio sink (LGPL-2.1-or-later), built from `tools/directaudio/sink`. - The DroidDeck HUD is [@The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner)'s [FusionHUD](https://github.com/The412Banner/FusionHUD) (GPL-3.0 with an attribution term). Its readings match Valve's [MangoHud](https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud) build (MIT), with frame times from gamescope patch 0125. - The HUD's CPU, GPU load, thermal and battery readers come from [@xXJSONDeruloXx](https://github.com/xXJSONDeruloXx)'s work. - LSFG frame generation comes from Camille LaVey and the [Eden](https://eden-emu.dev) project, following [lsfg-vk](https://github.com/PancakeTAS/lsfg-vk), ported by [@maxjivi05](https://github.com/maxjivi05). It needs your own copy of [Lossless Scaling](https://store.steampowered.com/app/993090/) and ships none of its shaders. - Black frame insertion follows the design of [@artzox](https://github.com/artzox)'s [BFI Presenter](https://github.com/artzox/BFI-Presenter) (GPL-3.0): the strobe runs on the display's refresh clock and the game is paced to the lit refresh. Both build on [Blur Busters](https://blurbusters.com)' research on MPRT and motion blur. No BFI Presenter code is used. - Remote Play decodes through Android's MediaCodec or the [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) (LGPL-2.1-or-later) in Steam's runtime. Qualcomm low latency settings follow [Moonlight](https://github.com/moonlight-stream/moonlight-android) (GPL-3.0). - [PipeWire](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/pipewire) (MIT) sockets use the settings in its `module-access.c`, and [WirePlumber](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pipewire/wireplumber) (MIT) keeps those clients at full permissions.
Desktop - The KDE pacman repository snapshots [Arch Linux ARM](https://archlinuxarm.org) and installs with [pacman](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/pacman/pacman) (GPL-2.0-or-later). - [KWin](https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kwin) (GPL-2.0-or-later) is patched to pass on the scroll data its `wayland_backend.cpp` leaves as a TODO. - Read without taking code: [Qt](https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtbase.git)'s `qwaylandinputdevice.cpp` and `qguiapplication.cpp`, [Konsole](https://invent.kde.org/utilities/konsole)'s `TerminalDisplay.cpp`, and [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa)'s `u_threaded_context.c` and `zink_resource.c`. - The Steam Keyboard window rule follows Valve's `steamdeck-kde-presets` with [Bazzite](https://github.com/ublue-os/bazzite)'s `0001-steam-virtual-keyboard.patch`. - Steam's Browse buttons open a GTK 3 file chooser via PyGObject (LGPL-2.1-or-later), shown over Steam by [gamescope](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/gamescope) (BSD-2-Clause) through `GetAppIdFromReaper`. - The AYN Odin 2 phantom second display was confirmed by [@SapphireRhodonite](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite)'s [WatermelonDS 0.0.5](https://github.com/SapphireRhodonite/WatermelonDS/releases/tag/0.0.5) notes and [iiSU #363](https://github.com/iisu-network/iiSU/issues/363), without taking their code.
Smart glasses - Builds on WinNative's VITURE work. Protocol checked against [@wheaney](https://github.com/wheaney)'s [XRLinuxDriver](https://github.com/wheaney/XRLinuxDriver), [@badicsalex](https://github.com/badicsalex)'s [ar-drivers-rs](https://github.com/badicsalex/ar-drivers-rs) and [go-macos/iokit](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-macos/iokit/viture). The optional VITURE SDK is not included. - The VITURE protocol V2 frames adapt [@elasticjava](https://github.com/elasticjava)'s [viture-v2](https://github.com/elasticjava/viture-v2) (MIT) by Holger Bartnick. See `docs/third-party/viture-v2`. - RayNeo adapts [@informalTechCode](https://github.com/informalTechCode)'s [RayNeo-Air-Series-3DoF-Scaffold](https://github.com/informalTechCode/RayNeo-Air-Series-3DoF-Scaffold) (Apache-2.0) and references [@verncat](https://github.com/verncat)'s [RayNeo-Air-3S-Pro-OpenVR](https://github.com/verncat/RayNeo-Air-3S-Pro-OpenVR) (MIT) and [Monado](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/monado/monado) (BSL-1.0). See [docs/third-party/rayneo](docs/third-party/rayneo/README.md). - XREAL 1S references XRLinuxDriver and [xrealOneDeviceKit](https://github.com/wheaney/xrealOneDeviceKit) by @wheaney, [@rohitsangwan01](https://github.com/rohitsangwan01)'s [xreal_one_driver](https://github.com/rohitsangwan01/xreal_one_driver) (MIT) and [@0xcaff](https://github.com/0xcaff)'s [xr-tools](https://github.com/0xcaff/xr-tools). - Rokid follows ar-drivers-rs, @badicsalex's [Void Computing write-ups](https://voidcomputing.hu/blog/worse-better-prettier/) and Monado's Rokid driver. - REDMAGIC display findings draw on [@mekhontsev](https://github.com/mekhontsev)'s [MagicDesk investigation](https://github.com/mekhontsev/magicdesk/blob/main/docs/xr-resolution-fix.md) and [@Coding-BR](https://github.com/Coding-BR)'s [decompiled Nubia kernel](https://github.com/Coding-BR/android_kernel_nubia_sm8850_qwjujube).
VR, Joy-Con and hand tracking - Joy-Con VR ports the arm model from Google's [GVR SDK for Unity](https://github.com/googlevr/gvr-unity-sdk) (Apache-2.0) and adapts the hand skeleton from Valve's [OpenVR](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/openvr) `handskeletonsimulation` sample (BSD-3-Clause), which follows Moshi Turner's work in Monado. Index offsets come from Monado's `vive_poses.c` (BSL-1.0). - Joy-Con research: Linux's [hid-nintendo](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/hid/hid-nintendo.c) by Daniel J. Ogorchock, [@dekuNukem](https://github.com/dekuNukem)'s [Nintendo_Switch_Reverse_Engineering](https://github.com/dekuNukem/Nintendo_Switch_Reverse_Engineering), [SDL](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL) and AOSP. Checked against [ALVR](https://github.com/alvr-org/ALVR), [OpenComposite](https://gitlab.com/znixian/OpenOVR), [PSMoveSteamVRBridge](https://github.com/HipsterSloth/PSMoveSteamVRBridge), [@F8LEFT](https://github.com/F8LEFT)'s [JoyConVr](https://github.com/F8LEFT/JoyConVr), [@krnelpan1c](https://github.com/krnelpan1c)'s [Daydream-Controller-SteamVR](https://github.com/krnelpan1c/Daydream-Controller-SteamVR), [@yoyobuae](https://github.com/yoyobuae)'s [joyconvr](https://github.com/yoyobuae/joyconvr), [Moonlight](https://github.com/moonlight-stream/moonlight-android) and [Dolphin](https://github.com/dolphin-emu/dolphin). See [docs/third-party/joycon](docs/third-party/joycon/README.md). - Camera hand tracking runs Google's [MediaPipe](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe) Pose Landmarker (Lite), BlazePose GHUM 3D and Hand Landmarker (Apache-2.0) on [CameraX](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/camera) frames (Apache-2.0), with usage reports off. Checked against JoyConVr's camera app (MIT). - Tracking math: the GVR arm model's accelerometer mode, Eric Foxlin's zero velocity updates, Frosio, Pedersini and Borghese's accelerometer autocalibration, a Kalman filter (Kalman, 1960), Horn's quaternion method (1987) and the 1€ filter (Casiez, Roussel and Vogel, 2012). - Gestures follow [ALVR](https://github.com/alvr-org/ALVR)'s `hand_gestures.rs` (MIT) and Meta Quest's menu pinch, tuned on [HaGRID](https://github.com/hukenovs/hagrid) photos (CC BY-SA 4.0, not included). - The glove model follows OpenVR's render model reference, is meshed with surface nets (Gibson, 1998; Mikola Lysenko), and uses Inigo Quilez's smooth minimum, distance field ambient occlusion and polygon distance (MIT). See [docs/third-party/handtracking](docs/third-party/handtracking/README.md).
## Star history
